paper.title: TEXEDO : Test Time Scaling for Controller-aware Language-conditioned Humanoid Motion Generation
paper.source_version: arXiv v2, revised 2026-06-23; current version checked 2026-08-31

decision_relevance.why_admitted: TEXEDO supplies a concrete reference-candidate interface, controller-grounded feasibility screen, feasibility-first selection rule, matched fixed-controller evaluation, and explicit failure handling for choosing a reference upstream of a frozen policy tracker.
not_evidence_for: Mode graphs, transition guards, or recovery policies
Feasibility on controllers other than the labeled SONIC Unitree G1 stack
A dynamics certificate for arbitrary composed references
A matched real-robot improvement over the N=1 baseline

mechanisms.name: Black-box best-of-N reference sampling
mechanisms.description: A frozen language-conditioned generator draws N candidate whole-body trajectories from a prompt; downstream verifiers consume only the decoded motions rather than generator internals.

mechanisms.name: Controller-rollout feasibility labels
mechanisms.description: Offline MuJoCo rollouts through the frozen SONIC tracker label each reference with binary success, normalized tracking quality, and completed-reference progress.

mechanisms.name: Feasibility-first oracle quality
mechanisms.description: Q* assigns all binary-label successes above all failures when beta is less than 1/(1+alpha), while tracking quality ranks successes and progress times tracking quality ranks failures.

mechanisms.name: Motion-only dynamic-feasibility surrogate
mechanisms.description: A causal temporal Transformer predicts success probability, tracking quality, and failure progress from the 36-dimensional reference trajectory and recombines them through the Q* form as R_dyn.

mechanisms.name: Robot-skeleton semantic co-embedding
mechanisms.description: Text and G1 motion encoders are contrastively trained so exponentiated negative embedding distance scores prompt-motion alignment independently of the dynamic verifier.

mechanisms.name: Feasibility gate then semantic rerank
mechanisms.description: Candidates with R_dyn above 0.8 form the admitted set; the most semantically aligned survivor is selected, or the maximum-R_dyn candidate is returned when the admitted set is empty.

mechanisms.name: Privileged exhaustive-rollout selector
mechanisms.description: The paper's Oracle baseline rolls out every candidate through SONIC and chooses the actual best candidate in the same finite pool, serving only as a deployment-impractical upper bound.

failure_modes.name: Candidate-pool coverage bound
failure_modes.description: Selection cannot recover a feasible, aligned motion when the frozen generator does not place one in the sampled pool; increasing N adds latency.

failure_modes.name: Tracker-specific feasibility model
failure_modes.description: Changing the tracker changes the executable set and requires new controller rollouts to relabel references and adapt the Dynamic Feasibility Verifier.

failure_modes.name: Least-bad fallback is not a feasibility certificate
failure_modes.description: When no candidate exceeds 0.8, the selector still returns the maximum-R_dyn candidate; this occurred on 1.18% of test prompts and can return a predicted-infeasible reference.

failure_modes.name: Imperfect surrogate-to-rollout agreement
failure_modes.description: Failure recall of 0.930 and overall Kendall tau of 0.656 show that the learned motion-only score is useful but cannot replace exact controller execution as certification.

failure_modes.name: Tracking errors condition on successful rollouts
failure_modes.description: MPJPE, velocity, and acceleration errors are averaged over successful rollouts only; reporting them without success and progress would hide early-termination failures.

failure_modes.name: No matched real-robot Base comparison
failure_modes.description: The hardware section reports 30 of 30 successful TEXEDO-selected trajectories but no N=1 Base row, so the hardware gain over unselected generation is not isolated.

failure_modes.name: Public selector diverges from the paper rule
failure_modes.description: At official commit 8c5beb5, the selection script linearly combines dynamic reward with z-normalized semantic distance instead of implementing the paper's thresholded filter-then-rerank rule and empty-set fallback.

failure_modes.name: Controller-label pipeline is not publicly reproducible
failure_modes.description: The public reproduction guide states that the rollout labels needed to retrain the dynamic verifier are absent, so adapting the released verifier to Sam's MDP requires building a new exact rollout-label path.

evaluation.name: In-distribution feasibility and alignment balance
evaluation.description: Against N=1 Base, N=32 TEXEDO reports success 0.873 to 0.984, VLM-Judge 5.722 to 6.054, MPJPE 44.34 to 39.09 mm, and Q* 0.829 to 0.926.

evaluation.name: Physical and semantic objectives conflict
evaluation.description: At N=32, dynamic-only selection reaches 0.990 success but lowers VLM-Judge to 4.924; semantic-only reaches VLM-Judge 6.110 but only 0.885 success, motivating gated composition.

evaluation.name: Dynamic-surrogate agreement with controller rollouts
evaluation.description: On held-out data the success head reports AUROC 0.979, AUPRC 0.997, and failure recall 0.930; within-prompt Kendall tau with exact Q* is 0.656 overall.

evaluation.name: Zero-shot transfer to Kimodo
evaluation.description: With no verifier retraining, Kimodo plus TEXEDO reports success 0.954 and VLM-Judge 5.381 versus 0.937 and 4.823 for one Kimodo sample.

evaluation.name: BONES-SEED prompt generalization
evaluation.description: On 50 OOD prompts, TEXEDO reports success 0.980, VLM-Judge 4.401, and Q* 0.942 versus Base values 0.860, 4.116, and 0.804; adjacent prose rounds TEXEDO Q* to 0.943.

evaluation.name: Physical Unitree G1 execution
evaluation.description: All 30 TEXEDO-selected references completed on hardware; frame-weighted MPJPE, velocity error, and acceleration error were 37.41 mm, 4.35 mm/frame, and 2.67 mm/frame squared, without a matched Base hardware row.

evidence.claim: arXiv v2 was submitted 2026-06-23 and is the current version checked on 2026-08-31.
TEXEDO samples decoded candidate reference trajectories from a black-box frozen generator and leaves the deployment-time tracker frozen.

evidence.locator: Section III-B, Equations 1-2; Appendix C-A, SONIC roll-outs and ordering guarantee
evidence.claim: Offline SONIC rollouts produce success, tracking-quality, and progress labels that define Q* and supervise a motion-only Dynamic Feasibility Verifier.
The paper filters candidates at R_dyn greater than 0.8, selects the maximum semantic score among survivors, and falls back to maximum R_dyn; fallback occurs on 1.18% of test prompts.
Experiments use Unitree G1, frozen SONIC, a privileged exhaustive-rollout Oracle upper bound, independent physical and semantic metrics, and report N=32 timing on one A100-SXM4 40 GB GPU.
The in-distribution comparison reports Base, dynamic-only, semantic-only, and TEXEDO results, exposing the feasibility-alignment trade-off and the combined selector's performance.
The same verifiers are evaluated zero-shot on Kimodo and on 50 BONES-SEED OOD prompts; Table 3 reports OOD TEXEDO Q* 0.942 while prose states 0.943.
The paper defines the 36-dimensional, 50 Hz G1 motion representation, corpus split, FSQ tokenizer, Flan-T5 generator, and sampling configuration.
The appendix specifies the dynamic-verifier architecture and losses, proves binary-label feasibility-first ordering, and reports head accuracy and within-prompt rank fidelity.
The appendix defines early termination, success, progress, tracking errors, successful-rollout conditioning, and the eight-call VLM-Judge ensemble.
TEXEDO executes all 30 selected trajectories on a physical Unitree G1 and reports per-prompt and aggregate tracking errors without a matched N=1 Base hardware row.
Performance is bounded by candidate quality and latency; changing the tracker requires new controller rollouts and adaptation of the dynamic verifier.

evidence.locator: Function select, lines 27-46 at official commit 8c5beb5
evidence.claim: The released selection function uses alpha-weighted dynamic reward minus beta-weighted z-normalized semantic distance, not the paper's thresholded filter-then-rerank rule.

evidence.locator: Verifier training, lines 55-68 at official commit 8c5beb5
evidence.claim: The public release omits physics-rollout labels needed to retrain the dynamic verifier and instead ships a frozen checkpoint.
